summary: 219 findings from all 11 reviewers (every findings file passed validate-findings.ts; one persona spec type error fixed in ux-review/personas/data.ux.ts) clustered into 111 triage items: 63 fix items (by area: session 17, reveal 11, viz 12, notes 5, render 11, selftest 2, integration 5), 26 owner decisions, 20 deferred, 2 not a problem. No blocker survived re-rating; the majors cluster on phones (mobile WebKit lands screens scrolled past their heading, timed blocks start with their key or keypad off screen, a header that eats 40% of the viewport), on keyboard and screen-reader paths that lose focus or keys (practice, "Keep going" in a running block, reading Enter submitting the block), on the save loop (a chosen file silently ignored, no way to see earlier results, the results header describing only the latest visit), on data honesty in the charts (off-scale estimates collapsing into the centre, matrix options drawn at 0.70 scale, an unreadable share card) and on two benefit claims in the copy. Owner decisions cover names and casing, the privacy placeholders, resume, the clock and break policy, the facet model, what 0 SD means, the "ranges that overlap" sentence (gated), card emphasis, file names and the number-entry grammar.

items.title: On mobile WebKit a new screen or item opens scrolled past its heading and question
items.reason: Verified in code: Screen.svelte only calls heading.focus() on mount and relies on the browser to scroll; mobile WebKit keeps the old scroll offset. Evidence is measured in three configurations (iPhone 13, iPhone SE, Pixel control, desktop WebKit control). On the SE the first digit-span sequence is presented off-screen, which is a measurement problem, not only comfort.
items.problem: After a tap low on the page (confidence Continue, an interstitial Start) the next screen on the iPhone emulations opens at or near its maximum scroll: the h1 and the question are above the viewport (item 2: scrollY 942/942, question 664 px above). Chrome on Pixel and desktop engines land at the top.
items.fix: web/src/session/Screen.svelte onMount: when `focus` is true, call `heading?.focus({ preventScroll: true })` and then `requestAnimationFrame(() => window.scrollTo({ top: 0, left: 0, behavior: 'instant' }))` so the new screen is laid out before the scroll. Leave `focus={false}` (first screen of a page load) untouched: no focus, no scroll. Do not change which element takes focus (the h1 stays the focus target; UX-068 is the owner question about that). The block stages are handled in UX-002 (render).
items.tests: New web/src/session/Screen.dom.test.ts: stub window.scrollTo and requestAnimationFrame; mount Screen with focus=true → h1 is document.activeElement, focus was called with preventScroll, scrollTo({top:0}) called once; with focus=false neither happens. New e2e/ux-session.spec.ts on the `iphone` project: answer a Matrix & Series item with the page scrolled to the bottom, tap Continue on the confidence panel, then `await expect(h1(page)).toBeInViewport()` and `page.evaluate(() => scrollY)` is 0; repeat with `test.use({ viewport: { width: 320, height: 568 } })` and the Spatial interstitial Start.
items.acceptance: On the iphone project (390x664 and 320x568) every item and interstitial opens with its h1 in the viewport; chromium/webkit desktop unchanged; keyboard-session.spec still sees focus on the h1.
